{"id": "4:43/q39", "question": "What is the force of the preposition in wiping?", "turns_on": "The cited interpretations, reports, language arguments, and legal evidence differ.", "positions": [{"id": "4:43/q39/p1", "position": "It governs wiping without changing the object", "reasons": "ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 (author): The preposition باء may govern the verb or be absent without change of meaning; Sībawayh gives مسحت رأسه and مسحت برأسه, and the same alternation with the chest. ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 (الزمخشري): Al-Zamakhsharī asks how the al-Māʾida phrase فامسحوا بوجوهكم وأيديكم منه can require part of the earth when bare rock has no soil, and answers that من marks a starting point. SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 (author): The object being wiped is omitted here and stated in 5:6 with منه, so this wording is understood in light of that verse. | mentions 5:6 SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 (سيبويه): Alternatively, باء is transitive: Sibawayh records مسحت رأسه وبرأسه, like نصحته ونصحت له. BURHAN, d. 794 (author): The al-Māʾida wording adds منه after the phrase about wiping faces and hands; al-Nisāʾ does not. BURHAN, d. 794 (author): باء also appears with objects in examples such as بأيديكم, بالمودة, باسم ربك, and بأيكم المفتون; المفتون is a passive participle, not a verbal noun. | mentions 68:6, 76:6, 22:25, 23:20, 4:43 IBNASHUR-FULL, d. 1393 (author): Using bāʾ with the wiped areas, in wudu and tayammum, signals thorough wiping and prevents extending the concession beyond what is needed. TABATABAI, d. 1402 (روايات من طرق أهل السنة): Several Sunni reports likewise say the verse preceded wine's prohibition; al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī allows that they may mean the prohibition of praying sluggishly. SAMARRAI-ASRAR (author): Al-Ma'idah details the full ablution and tayammum rulings, so it adds “from it” for clarification; al-Nisa' gives only some rulings and aptly leaves the phrase out. KASHSHAF-FULL (source note KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p547/r1) supports this position. KASHSHAF-FULL (source note KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p547/r2) supports this position. KASHSHAF-FULL (source note KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p547/r3) supports this position."}, {"id": "4:43/q39/p2", "position": "The bāʾ is connective or emphatic", "reasons": "NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 (author): The preposition bāʾ in the wiping phrase is said to be extra. SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 (أبو البقاء): بوجوهكم attaches to امسحوا; Abu al-Baqa regards the preposition باء as extra."}]}
{"id": "4:43/q40", "question": "What do God's names at the close convey?", "turns_on": "The cited interpretations, reports, language arguments, and legal evidence differ.", "positions": [{"id": "4:43/q40/p1", "position": "The names explain the concession and ease", "reasons": "BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 (author): God’s forgiveness explains the eased rule and dispensation. NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 (author): God is ʿafuww by granting concessions and ease, and ghafūr by pardoning error and shortcoming. ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 (الزمخشري): Al-Zamakhsharī takes the divine description as an allusion to legal concession and ease: God forgives and pardons, so He chooses ease over hardship. BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 (author): Ghafūr adds erasure of the sin; the author connects this to the tayammum concession, which makes prayer virtuous instead of leaving it or praying without purification. BURSEVI, d. 1127 (author): God’s pardon and forgiveness explain and affirm this permission and ease: His constant practice is to pardon sinners, so He makes matters easier rather than harder. ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 (author): The divine names explain and affirm the dispensation: God's settled practice is to pardon those at fault and forgive sinners, so He provides ease. ALUSI-FULL, d. 1270 (author): Al-Alusi says the facilitation sense in the hadith is not certain, and it is unlikely that forgiveness here specifically concerns those who prayed intoxicated and their recitation. MUQATIL (source note MUQATIL:4:43/r12) supports this position. TAB-FULL (source note TAB-FULL:v7p97/r1) supports this position. TAB-FULL (source note TAB-FULL:v7p97/r2) supports this position. ZAJJAJ (source note ZAJJAJ:v2p55/r9) supports this position. IBNABIHATIM (source note IBNABIHATIM:v3p962/r7) supports this position. IBNABIHATIM (source note IBNABIHATIM:v3p962/r8) supports this position. JISHUMI (source note JISHUMI:v2p1567/r30) supports this position. KASHSHAF-FULL (source note KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p547/r4) supports this position."}, {"id": "4:43/q40/p2", "position": "God pardons and covers sins", "reasons": "TABRISI, d. 548 (author): Ghafūr describes God as frequently covering the sins of His servants. TABRISI, d. 548 (قيل): An alternative gloss takes ʿafūw as abundant pardon and forbearance. IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 (الخطابي): Al-Khaṭṭābī says ʿafuww is an intensive form and means pardoning sins and leaving the wrongdoer unpunished. IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 (author): Another explanation derives the word from wind erasing a trace: the pardoner wipes away sins through pardon. QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 (author): God has always accepted pardon and been gentle, covering sin’s punishment rather than punishing. ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 (author): Abū Ḥayyān criticizes al-Zamakhsharī for accepting the apparent sense here despite usually distorting wording for his school, and for speaking of forgiveness without the repentance qualification he usually requires. IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 (author): The Prophet may have ordered wudu and prayer as repentance, as in the report that a sinner who performs wudu and two rak‘as is forgiven, cited at Quran 3:135. | mentions 3:135 IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 (author): God’s pardon includes legislating tayammum and allowing prayer with it when water is absent, as mercy, leniency, and relief."}]}
